description: Status checks are deliberately NOT skipped. CI (unit, lint, the privileged integration tests) passing is the only thing standing between an automerged bump and a broken router.

platformAutomerge is on, which hands the merge to GitHub so a PR lands the moment its last check goes green. This is only safe because the main ruleset marks every CI check required; without that GitHub would treat a PR as mergeable the instant it opened.

Actions are pinned to commit SHAs. A tag like v7 is mutable, so a compromised or retagged action would land in this pipeline without any config change here. Renovate keeps the SHAs current and writes the version alongside as a comment.
Base images are pinned to digests for the same reason: golang, distroless and debian:trixie-slim are rebuilt in place, so the bytes behind a tag change without any commit here.
gomodTidy is required because Renovate updates go.mod and go.sum with go get, which never prunes. CI fails on the tidy check otherwise.

customManagers.description: The k3s image of the k3s test.
The Renovate validator CI runs, and kubeconform.
BIRD, built from source in images/bird: the tag and its commit move together (the build checks one against the other).
The BIRD image the chart deploys (tag = BIRD version, plus digest). Published by bird-image.yaml after an images/bird change.
The git-sync image the autopeer chart runs (helm-values is off for charts/).
make lint pins the same golangci-lint as ci.yaml.
controller-gen generates the CRD; CI checks the committed output with the same version.

packageRules.description: The chart's images: helm-values would write digests into the tag fields. The BIRD image has its own manager (tag + digest), and the operator image digest is set by the release workflow.

The go.mod toolchain is what CI tests with and the golang image is what the images compile with (two Dockerfiles), so they move in one PR. make toolchain.verify fails the PR until all have landed in it.
Move golangci-lint in ci.yaml and the Makefile together, so local lint and CI never disagree.
The Kubernetes libraries are released together and will not compile apart, so update them as one PR.
0.x modules where a minor bump is a Kubernetes release and routinely needs code changes. Review them rather than automerging.

BIRD itself. Stay on BIRD 2 (3 is a different daemon); a patch of the current minor and a newer minor are separate PRs, so a fix never waits on a minor upgrade. Review every release by hand: it changes the router, and the dn42-bird DaemonSet only restarts by hand.
The BIRD image the chart deploys. Never automerged: every BGP session restarts when the dn42-bird pods are next deleted (OnDelete), so a new BIRD or rebuild is reviewed.
The BIRD image's Debian base only brings libraries and iproute2 now; digest updates can automerge like the others, a new Debian release is reviewed.
Action and base-image digests are safe to take unattended once CI is green.
